editorial.headline: Government Residential Care for Older People and People with Physical Disabilities
editorial.standfirst: This is government-run residential care for people who cannot manage their own daily lives and do not wish to live independently.
editorial.body:
This activity covers residential personal-care services run by government for older people and people with physical disabilities who are unable to look after themselves and do not wish to live independently. It is not simply accommodation: the setting brings care into the texture of daily life, with rooms, meals, supervision, safeguarding and household support forming part of the facility’s offer. Nursing services may also sometimes be provided to patients in a separate location.

The defining feature is therefore both the client group and the operator. The record identifies this as a government-managed activity, centred on residents whose needs make independent living unsuitable or unwanted. Its practical scope is deliberately broad enough to include the residential environment around the individual, rather than reducing care to a single clinical service. The presence of food, lodging, oversight and day-to-day assistance matters because these are part of the stated care setting, not incidental extras.

Nationally, the position for foreign investment is closed. The maximum foreign ownership shown for this activity is 0%, and the record lists no business scales as open. For a founder considering a foreign-owned structure, that conclusion is direct: this is not an activity available for foreign ownership at the national level. The governing source cited in the record is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

Bali does not soften that conclusion. The Bali status is closed, and the record marks PMA registration as blocked. Under these conditions, a foreigner cannot register this activity in Bali today. There is an important distinction in the local note: the activity is characterised as medium-high/high risk and is not blocked by Bali’s permanent island-wide moratorium on low and medium-low risk activities; the record says the position should be verified for the specific address. That is not an opening for PMA registration, but a reminder that the moratorium is not the reason recorded for this activity’s Bali position.
